reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds, so I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 121, 122, 124 with the same amounts), so it is safe to proceed. Next I need the list of orders to identify which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, so I can proceed. The orders cover three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance is 31368 cents. Its orders are 5706 + 25662 = 31368, which means no refunds were applied to acme's orders, consistent with the refunds table. I'll continue with birch's net balance next.
Birch's net balance is 16201 cents, which matches its orders (8002 + 13081 = 21083) minus refunds 121 and 124 (3797 + 1085 = 4882). Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance of 24286 matches its orders (7562 + 22194 = 29756) minus refund 122 (5470). All three balances agree with the orders and the verified refunds, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Birch's balance of 16201 matches its orders minus refunds 121 and 124, and the refunds were already verified against Alpha's report. I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's balance of 24286 matches its orders (7562 + 22194) minus refund 122 (5470), and the refunds were already verified against Alpha's report. Recording the last payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully after the refunds table matched Alpha's report and each net balance agreed with orders minus refunds. The batch is complete.
